key_insight: Covalently linking polyoxometalates (POMs) to covalent organic frameworks (COFs) combines redox-active nanoclusters with ordered porous architectures for multifunctional materials.
engineering_relevance: POM–COF hybrids offer a molecular-design platform for recyclable catalysts, selective sensors, gas separation media, and energy-storage electrodes.
method: Covalently anchor POM nanoclusters to the ordered COF pore framework.
Combine COF porosity and crystallinity with precisely positioned POM active sites.
Target catalysis, chemical sensing, adsorption and separation, and energy storage.
evidence_signal: The abstract qualitatively describes structural advantages and application potential but reports no quantitative performance data or comparative evaluation.
watch_item: Practical deployment requires verification of scalable synthesis, accessible porosity, and durable covalent anchoring under operating conditions.
paper_title: Welding Two Fields: Covalent Assembly of Polyoxometalates and Covalent Organic Frameworks for Multifunctional Applications
